articles.title: ‘Wheel of Fortune’ Announcer Jim Thornton Fired by Sony
articles.summary: “Wheel of Fortune” announcer Jim Thornton has been fired from the game show, producer Sony Pictures TV confirmed. “Following a thorough investigation, Jim Thornton’s employment with ‘Wheel of Fortune’ has been terminated, effective immediately,” the studio said in a statement.
body: The alleged incident took place in May, when according to TMZ, a passenger informed a flight attendant about the chat screen on Thornton’s laptop. Authorities were waiting to question Thornton when his flight landed at LAX, and after they spoke to the Thornton he was given permission to leave.

Neither Thornton nor his lawyer have publicly addressed the allegations; an attorney who said they represented the announcer, Allison Hart, told TMZ that Thornton had “become active in suicide-prevention advocacy since losing a close family member to suicide two years ago and he has spent time visiting chat rooms offering support to individuals suffering from suicidal ideation.”

On Tuesday, Sony Pictures TV said that “we have recently been made aware of allegations concerning Jim Thornton. He has been suspended from ‘ Wheel of Fortune ’ and we are recasting while we conduct a thorough investigation.”

The announcer joined “Wheel” in 2010 after the death of the show’s previous announcer, Charlie O’Donnell, and has also worked as a substitute announcer on “The Price Is Right.” He’s also been the voice of “Celebrity Wheel of Fortune” on ABC.

articles.summary: It was a dark and stormy night for “Spider-Noir.” The Prime Video/MGM+ series, starring Nicolas Cage in his first-ever regular TV role, has been canceled after eight episodes and won’t return for a Season 2.
body: Sony notes that its oversight includes more than 900 Marvel characters associated with the Spider-Man franchise. The second series to come out of that partnership is already in development and is expected to be announced soon.

“Spider-Noir” was based on the Marvel Comics character Spider-Man Noir, and was adapted for television by Oren Uziel. The series takes place during the Great Depression and stars Cage as Ben Reilly, “a seasoned, down-on-his-luck private investigator in 1930s New York, who is forced to grapple with his past life following a deeply personal tragedy, as the city’s one and only superhero.”

Lamorne Morris (“New Girl”), Li Jun Li (“Sinners”), Karen Rodriguez (“The Hunting Wives”), Abraham Popoola (“Atlas”), Jack Huston (“Boardwalk Empire”), and Brendan Gleeson (“The Banshees of Inisherin”) also star.

articles.title: 15/18 A Place to Heal review – heartfelt docu-realist study of a French teen psychiatric facility
articles.summary: Venice film festival Director Cédric Kahn combines compassion with coolly detailed forensic scrutiny in this genre-challenging film which puts a troubled love triangle at the centre of the story.
body: Veteran French director Cédric Kahn brings us a movie in a classic French vein: a docu-realist study of an institution, in this case a state psychiatric facility for teenagers between 15 and 18; with scenes in treatment suites, recreation areas, dorms and interview rooms. It’s something to compare perhaps with Laurent Cantet’s The Class, or Nicolas Philibert’s On the Adamant, or Canadian film-maker Denis Côte’s That Kind of Summer.

Kahn’s film is powerful and committed, although sometimes the acting comes close to shouty improv youth theatre. The tone is of course one of compassion, combined with coolly detailed forensic scrutiny, though audiences might be intrigued at Kahn’s use of Purcell’s Funeral Sentences on the soundtrack, music notably used by Kubrick in A Clockwork Orange, a film in which delinquent youth are treated more roughly. Kahn himself plays one of the senior medical staff, part of the gallery of authority figures – doctors, nurses, orderlies, therapists and a nervous intern – who are almost as affected by the institutional drama as the troubled young people themselves.
points: Venice film festival Director Cédric Kahn combines compassion with coolly detailed forensic scrutiny in this genre-challenging film which puts a troubled love triangle at the centre of the story.

articles.title: ‘Like a tired boxer, battered by applause’: as Andrew Scott’s biopic premieres, Richard Eyre remembers Ian Charleson’s superb, near-death Hamlet
articles.summary: In 1989, the Chariots of Fire actor took on the incredible task of playing Shakespeare’s prince while terminally ill from Aids. This weekend sees the world premiere of Elsinore, a new film about the episode, itself heavily-tipped for awards.
body: Ian Charleson was one of the finest actors of his generation and an important figure in the fight for gay rights. Yet the extraordinary circumstances of his final performance as Hamlet, just months before his death, are less familiar.

Now, a new film is bringing that haunting production back to life. Elsinore, directed by Simon Stone and starring Andrew Scott as the Scottish actor, will premiere at Telluride this weekend before opening the London film festival in October.

Charleson was 40 and terminally ill with Aids when he was cast as Hamlet in Richard Eyre’s 1989 production at the National Theatre, after Daniel Day-Lewis abruptly left the role. Charleson had first played Hamlet 15 years earlier and persuaded Eyre to let him reprise it, despite the director’s misgivings about his health.
“Ian was very bright, very witty, mischievous,” Eyre told the Guardian. “He was beyond good-looking. He was beautiful, and he had a beautiful singing voice.”

articles.title: Gavin and Stacey star Rob Brydon's regret at turning down Dolly Parton interview
articles.summary: The comedian visited Dollywood in his BBC series Rob Brydon's Honky Tonk road trip.
body: Gavin and Stacey star Rob Brydon says he "regrets" turning down the chance to interview Dolly Parton after choosing to stay on a family holiday.
Brydon fronted the BBC documentary series Honky Tonk Road Trip, where he travelled across the American South to celebrate 100 years of country music.
In it he visited Dollywood, a theme park created by Parton, where Dolly's relatives had traced the lineage of the Parton and Owens sides to Wales.

He was told he could interview Parton if he returned after filming had ended, but chose to stay on his family holiday in Arizona - an opportunity he now wished he had taken because he never got to meet her before she died.

articles.title: Latcho Drom director Tony Gatlif dies aged 77
articles.summary: Film-maker acclaimed for his celebrations of Roma culture had been working on a ‘historical film project’ in Provence. Tony Gatlif, the French director of more than 20 films that mostly concentrated on celebrating Roma culture across the world, has died aged 77.
body: His family said in a statement to AFP that Gatlif died on Wednesday of “a health issue” while working on a “historical film project” in Arles in Provence, France. “The beauty of his films, his generosity, his joy, his poetry, and his love of music will remain with us forever.”
The statement, from his wife, children and grandchildren wished him “ Latcho Drom ”, a Roma phrase meaning “safe journey”.

Latcho Drom is also the title of Gatlif’s breakthrough 1993 film, a celebration of Roma music that moves from India to Spain, and which won the Un Certain Regard award at the Cannes film festival that year.

Gatlif had more success in 1997 with Gadjo Dilo, which featured Romain Duris as a Frenchman who is searching for a Roma singer in Romania; it won a Silver Leopard at the Locarno film festival and a César award for best original music.

articles.title: Queer Edward II review – funny, touching time capsule of Derek Jarman at work
articles.summary: Venice film festival: Filmed during the making of his queer royal feature, while the director was living with HIV, the candid footage includes uproarious scenes at a Cliff Richard rehearsal.
body: There could hardly be a more vivid time-capsule film about the publicly funded British arts scene in the early 1990s than this engrossing fly-on-the-wall documentary about Derek Jarman and his movie Edward II. Based on the play by Christopher Marlowe, it is about the 14th-century English king and his love affair with his court favourite, Piers Gaveston, with Steven Waddington and Andrew Tiernan as the leads and Tilda Swinton as Queen Isabella.

The “outing” debate now in fact looks very dated and this is the one moment where you can sense that Jarman thinks that the OutRage! protesters got it wrong by harassing and bullying Cliff Richard; we see him assuring his own team later that Tatchell gave them a real telling off for this. (Did Tatchell actually do anything of the kind? Or is that what Jarman felt ought to have happened?) It’s an absorbing and affecting portrait of a dedicated artist at work.

articles.title: ‘Wheel of Fortune’ Announcer Jim Thornton Fired
articles.summary: Thornton was suspended from the series on Tuesday, when it was also announced that Sony launched an investigation into unspecified allegations.
body: Jim Thornton, the longtime announcer for Wheel of Fortune, has been fired by Sony.

“Following a thorough investigation, Jim Thornton’s employment with Wheel of Fortune has been terminated, effective immediately,” a company spokesperson said in a statement shared with The Hollywood Reporter.

TMZ reported on Thursday that he was suspended after alleged pedophilia chatroom photos prompted an investigation. The outlet published photos they alleged were screenshots of Thornton’s laptop that were taken by a passenger on an American Airlines flight in May from Charlotte to Los Angeles.

The passenger who took the photos told TMZ she saw images and texts that made it appear to be a chatroom for pedophiles; that same passenger notified a flight attendant about the alleged messages, sharing the photos with them. The captain reportedly notified the authorities and he was questioned at LAX after the flight landed, but was free to leave, per TMZ.
points: Thornton was suspended from the series on Tuesday, when it was also announced that Sony launched an investigation into unspecified allegations.

articles.title: Steve Hilton Wants to Boost California’s Nightlife Economy If He Wins Governor
articles.summary: The Republican says he wants to audit rules related to live music, block parties, beer gardens and other events. Plus, create an "Office of Fun and Freedom."
body: Steve Hilton is proposing the creation of the “Office of Fun and Freedom,” a rapid-action team housed inside the governor’s office that would be dedicated to streamlining the permitting process for various forms of nightlife, events at small venues and block parties, The Hollywood Reporter has learned.

A conservative looking to restore “the rebel spirit of California”? According to a policy document viewed by THR, that’s exactly what Hilton, a British-born entrepreneur-turned-Fox News host, who has been endorsed by President Donald Trump, is looking to do.

“California should be the most fun place in America. We have incredible weather, beaches, lakes, mountains, parks, food, music and people from every part of the world,” reads the document on the proposed office. “Yet the killjoy politicians and bureaucrats who run state and local government too often seem determined to stop anyone from enjoying it.”
